obligation: Bank recall of a misdirected wire or ACH (funds response)
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (cancellation of a payment order); FBI IC3 BEC guidance
trigger: Money sent on fraudulent instructions: a buyer's closing wire (variant A) or an owner distribution from the property management escrow account (variant B)
deadline: Immediately on discovery. After the receiving bank accepts a payment order, cancellation needs that bank's agreement (670.211(3)), so minutes matter
notify: Variant A: the buyer calls their own bank; the brokerage alerts the title company and its own bank. Variant B: the brokerage's escrow bank fraud desk (recall request)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational, not a notification duty

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any BEC attempt or loss, regardless of amount
deadline: As soon as possible, the same day (voluntary; no legal deadline)
notify: IC3 at www.ic3.gov with full banking details; the buyer files their own complaint in variant A

trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of Florida residents (for example a name with a driver license or passport number, or an email address with the password to that account, 501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email (never from the compromised mailbox)
applies_at_this_tier: Likely - agent mailboxes usually hold client driver license images or similar data; counsel decides from the mailbox review. The deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) needs a primary or functional federal regulator's breach rules, which this brokerage does not have

obligation: Florida no-harm determination instead of individual notice
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the brokerage reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a mailbox that held no ID, Social Security, or account access data; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. The 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the notice to individuals, never to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the individual notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (possible if the shared files or the transaction platform are reached; one agent mailbox usually holds fewer)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the brokerage (inbound; MSP and SaaS vendors)
trigger: A breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (the MSP, the productivity suite, transaction platform, property management platform, or backup vendor)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination; contracts may set shorter times (24 hours requested from the MSP)
notify: The brokerage (Office Manager); the brokerage then gives the notices in subsections (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in the vendor list (POAM-009)

trigger: Affected clients who live outside Florida (about 25% of buyers)
notify: Residents and, where required, state attorneys general or regulators, under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of every affected person; counsel applies each state's law

obligation: Florida Real Estate Commission notice of an escrow dispute
citation: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-10.032(1)
trigger: A diverted or missing deposit leads to conflicting demands on funds in a brokerage escrow account, or the broker has good-faith doubt about who is entitled to them
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand or of the doubt; start a settlement procedure within 30 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the brokerage holds the deposit and demands conflict

citation: Cyber liability policy (contract), including the social engineering endorsement ($100,000 sublimit)
trigger: Suspected account takeover, funds transfer fraud, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

trigger: A client's claim, or a circumstance likely to lead to one, that the brokerage's handling of instructions caused a loss
deadline: Per policy (treat as prompt written notice)

trigger: Unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers acquired without authorization
deadline: No later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the brokerage is not a financial institution (P03 1.1). Would apply if it added settlement or loan services

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then); a micro brokerage is below the SBA size standard and unlikely to meet a proposed sector criterion. Recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering an extortion or ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the incident turns into extortion (POL-03 4.12); all U.S. persons

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the brokerage holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the brokerage holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
